name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a 4-pixel focus ring in the brand color on every interactive element that receives keyboard focus. This makes keyboard navigation visible to low-vision users without changing the visual design for mouse users. The trade-off is a tiny increase in layout shift for some elements, but the ring is thin enough to avoid layout breaks.

name: Reader
text: Risk: A 4-pixel ring risks blending into low-contrast backgrounds or small touch targets, breaking WCAG 2.2 AA. Better: Use a 3px solid ring with 3px outer glow in brand color—visible on any background, meets reduced-motion if animated at 0s. Settle with a live contrast test against all brand colors and a keyboard-only user trial.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a 3-pixel solid focus ring in the brand color with a 3-pixel outer glow, no animation. This meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast on every background, including low-contrast ones, and stays visible even on small touch targets. The trade-off is a slight increase in perceived size, but it’s necessary for universal usability.

name: Reader
text: Risk: A 3px solid ring with 3px outer glow risks creating a "halo effect" that enlarges touch targets beyond finger-friendly size, breaking mobile usability. Better: Use a 2px solid ring with 1px outer glow—still meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, but keeps targets compact. Settle with a live tap test on a 44x44px button at 1x zoom.
